title: Next.js instrumentation hooks need exclusion guards and thin dependencies
summary: Framework instrumentation hooks run in constrained startup contexts. Guard unsupported runtimes by exclusion, keep the hook thin, and prove it fires once in a production-equivalent start.
ai_value: Helps agents avoid bundling server-only runner graphs into framework startup hooks or skipping runtimes because an expected runtime variable is undefined.

contexts: a Next.js app adds or changes instrumentation startup hooks
the hook may execute in node and edge-like runtime contexts
the hook imports job runners, database clients, or other server-only graphs

trigger_signals.description: The guard only runs when a runtime value equals the expected supported runtime.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Guard by excluding known unsupported runtimes; an undefined value may still be the desired server runtime.

trigger_signals.description: The hook imports a large runner graph or server-only modules directly.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Move the heavy dependency behind a thin dynamic boundary or runtime-specific loader.

trigger_signals.description: Build or startup errors mention unsupported schemes or runtime-only modules from the hook path.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Treat the hook as a constrained startup surface, not a normal application module.

negative_signals.description: The hook is pure telemetry with no runtime-specific imports and has an explicit supported-runtime contract.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: The thin-hook trap may not apply, but still verify single-fire startup behavior.

negative_signals.description: Processed-count stillness occurs during a long transaction in an import job.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: That is an import progress signal, not an instrumentation stall; see progress-state-must-match-cursor-semantics.

common_wrong_assumptions: A startup hook can import anything a normal server route can import.
Undefined runtime means the hook is not running in the supported runtime.
A successful build proves the hook fires exactly once at startup.

first_checks.check: Build after adding or changing the instrumentation hook.
first_checks.why: Import-graph and runtime-boundary failures often surface only at build time.

first_checks.check: Start the app in the closest production-equivalent mode and verify the hook fires once.
first_checks.why: Development hot reload can hide missing or repeated startup behavior.

first_checks.check: Review imports from the hook entrypoint and move heavy/server-only graphs behind thin adapters.
first_checks.why: Thin hooks reduce runtime compatibility failures.

decision_rules.condition: The hook must skip unsupported runtimes.
decision_rules.then: Skip known unsupported runtime values and allow unspecified supported server startup when the framework uses that convention.

decision_rules.condition: The hook imports heavy or server-only implementation graphs.
decision_rules.then: Keep the hook as a small dispatcher and load runtime-specific work only inside the supported runtime.

decision_rules.condition: The hook cannot be proven to fire once in production-equivalent mode.
decision_rules.then: Add a safe diagnostic marker or test until single-fire startup behavior is observed.

do_not: Do not bundle background job runners or server-only module graphs directly into instrumentation startup hooks.
Do not assume positive runtime detection is reliable when the framework may leave it undefined.
Do not keep unrelated lease or import-resume lessons in this record; link those records instead.

agent_directives.preferred_next_step: Inspect the instrumentation hook as a constrained startup surface: exclusion guard, thin imports, production-equivalent single-fire proof.

risk.notes: This record is de-identified agent guidance. It does not authorize bypassing maintainer, security, publication, production, billing, data, permission, or destructive-action gates.

sources.supports: Item 21 was conditionally selected after narrowing to guard-by-exclusion and thin instrumentation hooks. The reshape provides three trigger signals, so it was published.
